codeReview.summary: I reviewed the mission context, AGENTS/shared-state files, the worker transcript skeleton, the handoff for session 2754358c-3126-44a3-9050-396637e445b9, and commit 0c7f9b5. The feature adds useful deployment CRUD coverage and build-status prevalidation, but it does not yet satisfy the upload/runtime-access parts of the feature or several required VAL-E2E assertions.

issues.description: `ArtifactUploadRoute` still behaves as a synchronous create endpoint: it directly calls `CreateUploadedArtifactBuild` and returns `201 Created` with `uploadBuildResponse` instead of returning the required `202` operation envelope. That does not satisfy VAL-E2E-022 / the feature contract, which requires polling an operation result for artifact uploads.

Uploaded artifact builds are persisted with build_strategy `"uploaded_artifact"`, while the feature and VAL-E2E-022 require `buildStrategy: "prebuilt_wasm"`. The constructed `BuildJob` also never sets `BuildStrategy`, so the returned build payload omits the required strategy even before it is reloaded from storage.

`DeleteDeployment` only marks the deployment/runtime rows as stopped/terminated in the database. There is no actual runtime shutdown call, and the runtime abstraction only exposes `Launch` (see `backend/janus-api/internal/core/runtime_launcher.go:36`). As implemented, DELETE cannot guarantee that the WASM process is terminated or that the old runtime endpoint stops serving, which violates VAL-E2E-024 and the feature's deletion/runtime-access requirements.

The new test suite is much narrower than the feature scope. It checks envelope/listing/guard behavior (for example at lines 125, 326, 409, 619, and 653), but it never verifies polling a deployment operation to a succeeded result with `result.deployment.status == "running"`, non-empty `runtimeEndpoint`, and `domainBinding`; it never exercises a successful source-bundle upload or artifact upload; it never proves runtime GET returns 2xx; and it never proves the runtime endpoint becomes unreachable after deletion. Because this feature is explicitly about end-to-end deployment/runtime verification, those missing checks are blocking review gaps.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill requires manual `curl.exe` verification and `interactiveChecks` entries, but this feature handoff recorded only `go test` / `go vet` commands and still marked `followedProcedure: true`. That mismatch made it easy for handler-only tests to stand in for the required runtime/upload verification.

summary: Review failed. The commit improves deployment handler coverage, but artifact upload still misses the required async/prebuilt_wasm contract, deletion does not actually terminate runtimes, and the added tests do not verify the end-to-end runtime access behaviors this feature was supposed to prove.
